learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how tiny typos in our DNA or missing chromosomes can lead to genetic diseases, and how scientists track them through family trees.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sudden, inheritable changes in the DNA sequence. Point mutations change a single base pair (e.g., Sickle-cell anemia). Frameshift mutations insert or delete bases, altering the entire reading frame.
A chart showing the inheritance of a trait over several generations. Squares represent males, circles represent females. Shaded shapes indicate the presence of the disorder.
Diseases caused by the alteration of a single gene. Examples include Hemophilia (sex-linked recessive blood clotting disorder) and Sickle-cell anemia (autosomal recessive).
Caused by the absence, excess, or abnormal arrangement of one or more chromosomes. Usually occurs due to failure of chromatids to separate during cell division (non-disjunction).
Down Syndrome: Trisomy 21 (three copies of chromosome 21). Klinefelter's Syndrome: XXY male. Turner's Syndrome: XO female (missing an X chromosome).

fun_activity.title: 🌳 Family Tree Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a basic pedigree chart for a trait like 'tongue rolling' in your family. Use squares for men, circles for women, and shade them in if they can roll their tongue!

exam_tips: 📌 In a pedigree, if a trait skips a generation, it is usually recessive. If affected children always have at least one affected parent, it is likely dominant.
📌 Color blindness and Hemophilia are 'X-linked recessive'. They affect males much more often than females because males only have one X chromosome.
📌 Be able to define Down Syndrome specifically as the trisomy of the 21st chromosome.
quick_recap: ⭐ A change in just one single amino acid (glutamic acid to valine) causes hemoglobin to collapse in Sickle-cell anemia.
⭐ Karyotyping is the process of pairing and ordering all the chromosomes of an organism, providing a genome-wide snapshot.
⭐ Mutagens are physical or chemical agents (like UV radiation or X-rays) that induce mutations.
